main_text.l: AD IOAN. IACOMOTVM Barrensem amicissimum, & in Ecclesia Geneuensi verbi Dei ministrum Th. Quatigranus Tempensis hoc μνη-μόσυνον dabat.

DElius Aonio decorat pede dū sacros poetas, Orbemque ducit versibus decentem: Et nitida meritum gestit caput impedire lauro, Superbientis præmio coronæ: Plurima demissum resonat lyra, nec graues la-borum, Pacisque belliquæ vrget officinas: Ereptósve duces Orco inuidet, auream perita Ciere chordam vocibus canoris.

At properat tibi, Phœbus amicior, implicare frontem Æterne vates laurea comante. Cuius deleuit reliquas nitor inuidendus, alma Vt nocte lucei sÿderum minores Inter pura faces Latonia. Principum, nec alter Maiore plectro cædibus madentes

page.notes: The initial D is a large decorative letter joined to "Elius". Greek words "μνημόσυνον" are reproduced as best read. Some letters in the verse are uncertain, such as "vrget", "inuidet" and "sÿderum"; the printed text is set in italic throughout, with the Greek and the heading in capitals.
